encounters.name: Wave Echo 2 · Mine tunnels
encounters.note: One stalking ochre jelly. Lightning and slashing can trigger its Split reaction; use current HP.

encounters.name: Wave Echo 3 · Old entrance
encounters.note: Ten stirges on the ceiling. Check awareness individually; attached blood loss happens at the start of each stirge’s turn.

encounters.name: Wave Echo 4 · Old guardroom
encounters.note: Nine skeletons assemble the round after a living creature enters; no cloak/password exception.

encounters.name: Wave Echo 6 · South barracks
encounters.note: Three hungry ghouls. Claw paralysis has an end-of-turn repeat save.

encounters.name: Wave Echo 8 · Fungi cavern
encounters.note: Poison-gas hazard, no creature XP. Crossing disturbs it; DC 11 Constitution, 3d6 poison and poisoned for 10 minutes on failure.

encounters.name: Wave Echo 9 · Great cavern
encounters.note: Seven ghouls on the western ledge react to light or noise. Ten-foot escarpments and stairs matter.

encounters.name: Wave Echo 11 · North barracks
encounters.note: Five loyal bugbears; eastern door barricaded. Listening can warn the party.

encounters.name: Wave Echo 12 · Smelter cavern
encounters.note: Eight zombies and one flameskull. Fireball and one-hour rejuvenation require deliberate tracking.

encounters.name: Wave Echo 14 · Mormesk
encounters.note: Adventure-specific 45-HP Mormesk. Bargain before harming him or stealing; maximum-HP drain must be recorded.

encounters.name: Wave Echo 15 · Forge guardian
encounters.note: Spectator parley is possible. DC 15 Deception can release it; do not automatically start combat.

encounters.name: Wave Echo 18 · Collapsed cavern
encounters.note: Three bugbears and Vhalak. Two bugbears begin in the rift; Vhalak may warn Nezznar after two bugbears die.

encounters.name: Wave Echo 19 · Nezznar
encounters.note: Nezznar, two temple bugbears, four giant spiders. Existing area-18 survivors may join after three rounds; never duplicate them.

runbookBeats.title: Session 6 · prepare the mine expedition
read: Before another journey, your equipment lies within reach: lamps to check, packs to close, provisions to count. The work ahead will take you beyond familiar doors and into stone where daylight cannot follow. You can still decide what to carry, whom to trust, and what you hope to bring back.

An expedition need not answer every question at once. You can set a limit on time, agree on a retreat signal, or choose a single objective before you enter. What is your purpose this time, and what would make you turn back?
run: Actual checkpoint: outside Barthen’s Provisions; Gundren left at an unnamed inn after being put to sleep; Trista holds the captured rat. Entry, payment, Gundren’s present condition and rat recognition remain unconfirmed.
DM-only: Glasstaff escaped to Cragmaw Castle. The party has not earned that destination. Keep this separate from a route to the castle and from the historical transfer of Gundren.
Use the current saved five character sheets. Do not refill HP, spell slots, hit dice, potion stock or other resources when opening a preparation package. Confirm a rest through the existing review.

Entry gate: an earned mine route, a decision to enter, and current sheets/resource review. A castle rumor alone is not a precise mine entrance. Verify actual map custody or other corroborated directions.
Use all 20 existing room cards, their actual exits and linked encounter cards. Establish light and marching order. Area 1 is the entrance; no fixed room sequence is required.

The printed mine assumes level 4 or higher. Use the actual mixed-level five-person party and current encounter review. Warn through observable danger and support retreat; do not silently change levels or add unearned rests.
Pacing suggestion: arrival 15–20 minutes; two or three connected rooms 60–90; one major fight or negotiation 45–60; retreat/close 15. Do not promise to finish Wave Echo Cave in one evening.

Nezznar, Nundro, the Forge, Mormesk and the spectator have independent situations. A choice to negotiate, bypass, retreat or return does not force a single ending. Keep city transition preparation future-only until mine outcomes are approved.
private: LMoP pp. 42–51. Wave Echo Cave may span several game nights.
runbookBeats.tv: Private preparation. Preview the selected player-safe visual, then use Show on TV. Browsing this card reveals nothing.

runbookBeats.title: Arrival · follow a route the party actually earned
runbookBeats.tv: Preview cave art before showing it. Reveal the journey-map destination only after the characters know the route.
read: The foothills close around the trail. Ahead, a dark opening cuts beneath the rock. Cold air brushes past you, and from somewhere below comes a low crash, like surf heard through the earth.

The opening offers a visible threshold, but the sound beyond it reaches farther than your sight. The rocky approach gives you a place to check equipment and gather your light before entering. You can study the ground, agree on your order, or listen for the next distant surge.
ask: Who leads, who carries the map, and what lights the way? Are you entering to rescue someone, confront the Spider, explore the mine, or all three?
run: The mine lies about 15 miles east of Phandalin in the Sword Mountains. Gundren’s map or another established source leads to area 1; possession of a rumor alone does not reveal a precise entrance.

General features: cold, damp, drafty; no light unless the room says otherwise. Tunnels are normally 10 feet high, rooms 20 feet, caverns 30 feet. Doors are heavy stone slabs; most passages have rough stone walls.
Use the private p. 43 plan for connections and distance: one printed square is 10 feet. The unmarked TV maps are interpretations. State the distance and exits when the art differs.
About every two minutes, a distant surge shakes the silence, louder toward the northeast. It comes from the subterranean water in area 16; it does not prove an Echo phenomenon.
Choose an actual passage after each room. Number order is a reference, not a required route.
Trista: offer a private choice about showing the rat or investigating it; never expose the BELOW token through narration.
Pebble: offer a practical packing, stonework or safe-footing contribution; ordinary rocks do not automatically grant a homebrew benefit.
Donavan: invite a sourced account or question for correspondence; separate testimony from his interpretation.
Ringgo: make bargaining, scouting and legitimate paid work useful alternatives to coercion.
Aldric: offer a choice to protect a vulnerable person or compare records; do not reveal his resurrection’s cause or Halaster’s involvement.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver pp. 42–44. Original read-aloud. Optional Echo atmosphere must remain labeled as a campaign addition.

runbookBeats.title: Area 1 · Rockseeker camp and the descent
runbookBeats.tv: Reveal the camp and visible pit. Cave-entrance art is E01; keep later rooms covered.
read: Three bedrolls surround a silent camp. Supplies lie where their owners left them. A dwarf’s body rests among the bundles, and a rope tied around a stone spire drops into a break in the cavern floor.

The rope is the clearest connection between this camp and the space below. Its fastening and the edge of the pit can be examined before anyone descends. The bundles and the body offer separate questions, and you can leave room for someone to keep watch while the others decide where to begin.
ask: Do you examine the camp, tend to the dead, secure the rope, or watch the passages below?
run: The dead dwarf is Tharden, Gundren’s brother, killed by Nezznar. Nundro was captured and is in area 20; the camp alone does not tell the characters his current location.
Useful ordinary provisions and mining equipment remain. Tharden wears boots of striding and springing; record discovery, identification, and ownership separately.
The pit is 10 feet wide and 20 feet deep. Without a rope, climbing its wall requires DC 15 Strength (Athletics). Failing by 5 or more causes a fall: 1d6 bludgeoning per 10 feet fallen, then prone.
From the pit bottom, the northwest passage leads to area 2; the east passage leads to area 3. The existing rope offers a practical way down; do not apply the no-rope DC to every descent.
choices: Northwest: mine tunnels, area 2.
East: old entrance, area 3.
Return to the surface using the actual secured route.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 44; marked map p. 43. Boots: appendix A. Do not show the corpse as Nundro.

runbookBeats.title: Area 2 · Mine tunnels
runbookBeats.tv: Reveal only reached branches. Do not place the lurking jelly on TV before it is seen.
read: Low passages cross and divide ahead of you. Tool marks stop abruptly at unfinished stone faces. Between the turns, even your footsteps seem to lose their direction.

The low stonework makes every turn feel close, and the unfinished faces give several branches a similar appearance. You can keep a mark at the last junction, follow the group carefully, or stop to compare the visible passages before choosing one. Your route back is something you can record as you go.
ask: How do you mark the route and keep one another in sight? Who watches behind?
run: These older workings have ceilings only 6 feet high. Several branches end at abandoned rock faces.
One ochre jelly lurks in a dead end. It stalks intruders and tries to catch a lone target. Use its actual movement and opportunities; it does not appear in several passages at once.
Review its Split reaction before resolving slashing or lightning damage. Track each resulting jelly’s identity and HP if it splits.
There is no keyed treasure here. Use the private map to adjudicate the maze rather than inventing forced wrong turns.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 44; ochre jelly appendix B. Stalking is printed behavior; specific movement depends on play.

runbookBeats.title: Area 3 · Old entrance and ceiling stirges
runbookBeats.tv: Show the carved hall and bones; reveal the stirges only after detection or their attack.
read: Carved miners still work along the walls above a floor strewn with ancient bones. Empty brass lamps hang in the stone. Beyond them, the high ceiling disappears into shadow.

The abandoned lamps offer no light of their own. Your illumination catches the miners' carved tools and the pale bones at different heights, leaving the upper space harder to judge. You can inspect the floor, examine the figures on the walls, or direct your attention toward the ceiling.
ask: Are you studying the carvings, searching the bodies, watching the ceiling, or passing through?
run: Ten stirges cling to the 30-foot-high ceiling. Roll one Dexterity (Stealth) check for the group and compare it with each character’s passive Perception if that character is not watching the ceiling; resolve active observation normally.
Use the 2014 surprise procedure individually for any creature that failed to notice the threat. Characters who detect them hear flapping as the attack begins.
The bones are remains of miners and invaders, not another skeleton encounter. Track attached stirges on their specific targets and remove them when detached or slain.
The old southern entrance was buried long ago. It is not a usable shortcut to the surface without a separately planned excavation.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 44. Room 3 holds ten stirges; the nine animating skeletons are in room 4.

runbookBeats.title: Area 4 · Old guardroom
runbookBeats.tv: E04 shows the room; stage E04B only when the bones rise. Do not reveal the ambush image at entry.
read: Stone bunks and splintered racks lie beneath a fallen section of ceiling. Bones are scattered between them, half buried in pale dust.

The bunks identify this as a place where people once slept, while the broken racks suggest equipment no longer fit for use. Fallen stone interrupts parts of the floor. You can study the room from the threshold, choose a route through the debris, or examine a particular set of remains.
ask: Who enters, and where is everyone when you begin looking around?
run: In the round after a living creature enters, the remains assemble into nine skeletons. Start combat at that trigger; they do not rise before someone enters.
The skeletons fight until destroyed. Keep survivors recorded if the party withdraws; a later visit does not create nine new skeletons.
Rubble and broken furniture can affect movement or cover only where actually present. No treasure is keyed here.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 44. Original narration avoids announcing the animation before its trigger.

runbookBeats.title: Area 5 · Assayers’ office
runbookBeats.tv: Show E05 and the entered room. Keep strongbox contents private until opened.
read: Three dusty scales stand on a stone counter. Paper scraps fill small niches behind it, and the floor holds the remains of workers and warriors who never left.

The arrangement of the scales and niches suggests work that once involved careful measurements and records. The scraps are within reach, but their age is visible in their edges. You can look without touching, search the counter, or ask someone who knows the writing to examine what survives.
ask: Do you inspect the papers, counter, or bodies? Who handles the old records?
run: The papers crumble when touched. Someone who reads Dwarvish can make out remnants of ore weights and payments; there is no complete surviving ledger to take.
A locked iron strongbox sits behind the counter. Opening its lock requires thieves’ tools and DC 20 Dexterity.
Contents: 600 cp, 180 sp, 90 ep, and 60 gp. Add only money actually collected to party inventory; record an unopened or emptied box for the return visit.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver pp. 44–45. No combat group is keyed to this office.

runbookBeats.title: Area 6 · South barracks
runbookBeats.tv: Use E06 after the interior is visible. Do not announce the creatures through a closed door.
read: Rows of stone bunks flank an old brazier. Three gaunt shapes crouch over the scattered bones, working their jaws against scraps far too old to feed them.

The bunks and old brazier break the chamber into narrower gaps than its size first suggests. The shapes among the bones are occupied with what lies before them. You can stop at the entrance to judge those gaps, choose where to stand, or decide whether to make your presence known.
ask: Do you listen first, slip past, draw them out, or enter?
run: Listening at the partly open door: DC 10 Wisdom (Perception) hears crunching and splintering.
Three ghouls attack fresh prey immediately. They belong to the larger pack whose other seven members occupy area 9; these are separate starting groups, not replacements.
Review claw paralysis, the creature’s immunity exceptions, and end-of-turn saves. Mark a paralyzed target so subsequent attacks are resolved correctly.
If a pursuit moves these three elsewhere, update their location instead of deploying them again.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 45; ghoul appendix B. No treasure is keyed here.

runbookBeats.title: Area 7 · Ruined storeroom and a secure rest
runbookBeats.tv: Show E07. This is an opportunity to pause without a new enemy reveal.
read: A collapsed wall opens onto a small chamber. Beyond a half-open door, a surviving storeroom holds neat rows of cracked, empty kegs. Its stonework is sound.

The half-open door breaks the line of the collapsed wall. Beyond it, cracked kegs still stand in something like their old order, a small island of storage amid the ruin. The sound of stonework carries here; its source remains out of sight.
ask: Do you inspect and secure the door? Who keeps watch, and are you taking a short rest or settling in longer?
run: The northern storeroom is a secure resting place: the adventure explicitly says monsters do not come here. Its sound door can be blocked or barred from inside.
Do not roll routine wandering attacks inside this refuge. If the party knowingly leads an active pursuer here, resolve that specific pursuit openly before calling it secure.
The kegs are empty. Track rest duration, recovery choices, light, and ongoing conditions through the rest controls. A rest does not revive defeated enemies or replace taken treasure.
choices: Use the Rest / retreat card to review recovery and the expedition record.
Continue through an already explored route after the players choose.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 45. The secure-room exception overrides general wandering guidance. Rest rules use the campaign profile and recorded character exceptions.

runbookBeats.title: Area 8 · Fungi cavern and poison gas
runbookBeats.tv: E08 before disturbance; E08B only after gas is released. Stage affected characters before resolving saves.
read: Pale caps, thick stalks, and shelves of fungus crowd the cavern. Some growths glow green, casting enough light to reveal the far wall. The floor between them is almost lost beneath the carpet.

The faint green light clings to the caps and stalks, leaving the room's edges hard to judge. The growth covers the walking surface as well as the view ahead. Before crossing, you can study its spread from the threshold and decide how close to bring your light.
ask: How do you cross without disturbing the growth? Do you test the air, scout a route, or seek another passage?
run: Most fungi are harmless, and the glow lights the whole cavern. Attempting to cross disturbs the carpet and releases poison gas.
Each creature in the cavern makes DC 11 Constitution: failure deals 3d6 poison and causes Poisoned for 10 minutes; success avoids these effects. Do not apply half damage on success.
Gas disperses after 1 minute. Until then, each living creature ending its turn in the cavern repeats the save. Review poison immunities and resistances separately for each target.
The book does not give a fixed DC for every invented crossing method. Decide whether the plan avoids disturbance before rolling, state any ruling, and preserve player alternatives.
Record gas start/end time and each character’s condition. Pebble’s mineral interest is not evidence that this fungus is edible or that an unconfirmed ancestry trait grants poison immunity.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver pp. 45–46. Gas is a hazard, not a creature and not a compulsory fight.

runbookBeats.title: Area 9 · Great cavern
runbookBeats.tv: Stage the dedicated cavern map with unreached ledges hidden. E09 is the room illustration.
read: The hall opens around long stone tables and cold braziers. Stairs climb to ledges at either end, above a floor scattered with the remains of an ancient battle.

Cold braziers offer no warmth to the long tables. The stairs and ledges at either end rise above the scattered remains, giving the chamber more than one level to watch. Anything moving across the open floor would be difficult to overlook from above.
ask: What light or noise have you brought? Do you cross the lower floor, climb a ledge, or watch the shadows first?
run: Seven ghouls lurk on the western ledge. They notice light or noise elsewhere in this cavern and rush down to attack; they fight until destroyed.
The escarpments are 10 feet high. Climbing requires DC 12 Strength (Athletics). Falling or being knocked from the top deals 1d6 bludgeoning and leaves the creature prone.
Keep elevation, stairs, and routes of retreat visible on the DM map. These seven are additional to the three initially in area 6; reconcile any actual movement between groups.
The scale and stair positions come from the private p. 43 plan when the painted close-up differs.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 46. Seven ghouls plus terrain can be very dangerous to the current party.

runbookBeats.title: Area 10 · Dark pool
runbookBeats.tv: Show E10 and the pool; do not announce its submerged treasure before investigation.
read: Still black water fills the cave. Pale broken shells crunch along the bank, and a slow stream slides away beneath a low opening to the northeast.

The bank's shells crunch beneath a careful step, while the black water gives little sense of its depth. The stream's low northeastern opening draws your eye away from the pool. Following it would mean approaching stone and water that conceal what lies beyond.
ask: Do you sound the depth, secure a rope, search underwater, or follow the stream?
run: The pool reaches 20 feet deep in the middle. The northeast stream is 3 feet deep, with only 2–3 feet of air above it; characters can wade along it to area 18.
Searching the pool reveals a skeleton on the bottom, 10 feet from shore under 10 feet of water. It is a former human wizard, not an active monster.

The skeleton has two platinum rings worth 75 gp each and a wand of magic missiles. Resolve actual underwater movement, air, retrieval, and identification; do not require an invented Perception DC just to replace the keyed discovery.
Record who has the wand and its charges before use. Show any discovery handout only after it is retrieved.
choices: The northeast stream reaches the collapsed cavern, area 18.
The stairway east reaches the north barracks, area 11.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 46; marked map p. 43; wand in appendix A.

runbookBeats.title: Area 11 · North barracks
runbookBeats.tv: Use E11 after entering. Reveal only the defenders actually still stationed here.
read: Heat from a glowing brazier touches your face. Stone bunks line the walls, and a broken table has been piled against the eastern door.

The brazier's warmth sets this room apart from the colder passages. Bunks leave narrow spaces between them, and the broken table piled against the eastern door makes that exit a practical obstacle. You can inspect the barricade from this side before deciding whether to disturb it.
ask: Do you listen, approach under a pretext, force the barricade, or find another route?
run: Five bugbears serve Nezznar here and hold back the undead. Listening at either door with DC 10 Wisdom (Perception) hears hungry voices speaking Goblin.
The eastern door is barricaded from within: DC 20 Strength to force it. The west door is not given that barricade.
The largest bugbear carries 15 cp, 13 ep, and a potion of vitality. This is vitality, not a healing potion; use its actual item effects.
Bargaining, misdirection, and withdrawal remain possible if the players attempt them; the book gives no automatic friendly bargain. Track anyone sent elsewhere rather than spawning a replacement.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 46. These five are separate from the three in area 18 and two with Nezznar.

runbookBeats.title: Area 12 · Smelter cavern
runbookBeats.tv: Show E12 when the skull is visible; use the smelter map for channel depth and targets.
read: A cold furnace towers above abandoned ore carts. Beside it, a motionless wheel hangs over a dry channel. Green fire dances around a skull suspended above the armored dead.

Ore carts stand idle beside the furnace, and the wheel hangs motionless over a dry channel. Green fire outlines the skull and catches on the armored dead. The old machinery divides the floor into working spaces; the threat now occupies the same ground where miners once labored.
ask: Do you retreat from the guardian, attempt to speak, use the channel, or engage? How closely are you standing together?
run: Eight corpses are zombies. They rise against living creatures entering the room but pursue outside it for no more than one round. One flameskull follows its ancient order to prevent intruders passing.
Review the flameskull’s spell card before combat: its area damage is a major danger. Preserve actual spell use, concentration, defenses, and targets; do not grant unlimited fireballs.

A destroyed flameskull reforms after 1 hour unless its remains receive holy water, dispel magic, or remove curse. Record which method was used and the deadline; merely reducing HP to 0 is not permanent clearance.
The dry channel is 10 feet wide and its floor 5 feet below the room. No ability check is needed to scramble in or out. It runs north and east; beyond the room its ceiling is only 5 feet high.
Area 17 provides another route around these guardians. Do not force the party to win this encounter to reach the Forge.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 46; flameskull appendix B. Rejuvenation is a creature rule. Record actual destroyed remains and treatment for the return trip.

runbookBeats.title: Area 13 · Starry cavern
runbookBeats.tv: Show E13. Keep the interiors of buildings 14 and 15 covered.
read: Your light scatters across a ceiling that glitters like a field of stars. Below it stand two battered stone buildings, blackened by fire, amid the fallen dead.

Points of light prick the ceiling above the two blackened buildings. Down below, fallen bodies and scorched stone tell a harsher story. The buildings interrupt the open cavern, each offering a closer approach and a separate interior to examine.
ask: Do you inspect the stone, examine the buildings, or look for the source of the lingering magic?
run: The ceiling’s minerals are attractive but neither magical nor valuable. Do not silently turn Pebble’s taste for unusual stone into a magic-item reward.
A character proficient in Arcana senses subtle magic here; detect magic also reveals it. The aura strengthens toward the northern building, area 15.
The buildings use human proportions, unlike the dwarf-sized doors elsewhere. Area 14 is the former guest quarters; area 15 is the workshop.
No creature encounter or fixed treasure is keyed to this open cavern. If an actual wandering encounter occurs, use the wandering card and record it separately.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 47. The mine’s surviving magic has its printed explanation; the custom Echo story is not proven by this aura.

runbookBeats.title: Area 14 · Mormesk and the wizards’ quarters
runbookBeats.tv: Use E14 first; E14B when Mormesk manifests. Keep the chest and hidden map private until discovered.
read: Charred furniture stands beneath a sagging ceiling. A scorched chest waits beside a ruined bed. As you step in, darkness gathers out of the floor and turns toward you.

Charred furniture crowds the room beneath the damaged ceiling. The bed and chest survived the destruction well enough to recognize, though their contents cannot be judged from here. The dark presence near the floor draws attention away from them, making the threshold a useful place to stop and look.
ask: Do you answer the spirit, offer something, withdraw, or threaten it? Has anyone touched its possessions?
run: The damaged doors need DC 15 Strength to wrench or smash open. Mormesk the wraith rises when a living creature enters. He attacks if no one attempts to reason with him.
If neither he nor his property has been harmed, he listens. A useful magic item, scroll, spellbook, or arcane knowledge plus DC 10 Charisma (Persuasion) can persuade him of an offering’s value.

After accepting a gift, he permits examination of his books and lets the party keep the hidden map. He offers the coins and gems for killing the spectator in area 15, but never willingly gives up his wooden pipe.
Unlocked chest: 1,100 cp, 160 sp, 50 ep, three diamonds worth 100 gp each, and a platinum-decorated wooden pipe worth 150 gp. Reward access depends on the actual bargain or defeat.
DC 12 Intelligence (Investigation) reveals a map sewn into one preserved book. Its destination is a DM-created future dungeon; record your chosen location before publishing it.
Mormesk is dangerous and self-interested, not a trustworthy guide to the whole mine. Track Life Drain’s maximum-HP reduction if combat occurs.
choices: A gift can buy access without combat.
Rejecting his request to kill the guardian remains a valid choice.
A map can seed the next campaign chapter after the party chooses to follow it.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 47; wraith appendix B. Any Waterdeep or Echo destination assigned to the sewn map is a labeled campaign addition.

runbookBeats.title: Area 15 · Forge of Spells and its guardian
runbookBeats.tv: E15 shows the guardian, so display it only when the room can be seen. Use the close-up map if positions matter.
read: Scorched worktables ring a workshop that should have fallen silent centuries ago. Yet green flame still moves in a brazier at its heart. Above it, a many-eyed creature turns, and a greeting sounds inside your mind.

The brazier's green light colors the scorched tables, while the many-eyed creature hangs within the ruined workspace. Its greeting reaches you without crossing the air. There is room to answer before moving closer; the surviving forge equipment remains something to study rather than claim on sight.
ask: Do you speak to the guardian, study the fire, show credentials, or reach for something?
run: One spectator guards the workshop and still believes the mine operates. It does not attack merely because visitors speak; it attacks if they try to remove anything.

DC 15 Charisma (Deception) can convince it that one or more characters are wizards or miners authorized by the owners to end its employment. On success it returns to its home plane. Blinding it also makes it leave, believing it can no longer perform its task.
The north room’s door needs DC 15 Strength to force; the western double doors are damaged but slightly open. The northern workroom holds no additional keyed treasure.

DC 15 Intelligence (Arcana) identifies the brazier as the magical source. The depleted Forge cannot make permanent enchantments. A nonmagical weapon or armor bathed in its flame for at least 1 minute becomes +1 for 1d12 hours. The brazier cannot be removed.

The southeast table holds Lightbringer (+1 mace; commanded torch-like light; +1d6 radiant against undead while glowing) and Dragonguard (+1 breastplate; advantage on saves against dragon breath weapons). Claim only after resolving the guardian and record the actual bearer.
Use the Forge-use card for temporary items and expiry. Do not stack another +1 onto an already magical item or treat the fire as a permanent upgrade.
choices: Discharge the guardian through deception, depart peacefully, or fight if the party chooses.
Mormesk’s demand is optional; the spectator can leave without being slain.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 48. Negotiation, blinding, temporary enchantment, and the two named items are printed content. Any later Forge restoration project requires a separate campaign ruling.

runbookBeats.title: Area 16 · Booming cavern
runbookBeats.tv: Show E16 and only the ledge the party has reached. Keep water volume below table conversation.
read: The passage ends above churning water. A surge races through the dark and strikes beneath the ledge with a crash you feel in your chest. Then the water sinks back, leaving a long, hollow roar.

Each surge changes the sound of the cavern, filling the spaces between words before falling away again. The water and the stone around it are visible things to study. You can keep back from its edge, watch the rhythm, or inspect the route without entering the water.
ask: Do you watch a full cycle, test the ledge, enter the water, or turn back?
run: At normal level, the south ledge is 15 feet above water. A surge every 2 minutes raises the water 10 feet; after 1 minute it drops to its normal 20-foot depth.
The printed room has no automatic damaging wave attack or fixed swim DC. If characters enter, explain the current circumstances and adjudicate swimming, breath, rescue, and any stated ruling.
The sound suggests a larger cavern to the northeast, but that unkeyed continuation is not a prepared secret exit. Do not invent a safe passage without establishing it.
This is the physical source of the mine’s rhythmic booming. No Echo revelation is required to explain it.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver pp. 44 and 48–49. Water timing and dimensions are printed; any added current hazard is custom and must be announced consistently.

runbookBeats.title: Area 17 · Old streambed bypass
runbookBeats.tv: Show E17. Reveal the low route as it is explored rather than unveiling both ends at once.
read: A dry channel squeezes beneath a low ceiling. Smooth stones and rounded boulders mark the course water once followed through the dark.

Smooth stones lie among larger boulders in the dry channel. With the ceiling hanging low, the route asks you to watch both your footing and your head. Its bends and obstructions break the view ahead; you can keep track of the way back as you pass them.
ask: Who scouts the narrow passage, how do you carry light, and how do you help anyone slowed by the space?
run: The passage is only 4 feet high and strewn with rounded stones. Describe the restriction and apply squeezing only if a creature’s size and the actual passage dimensions require it.
This was an old route toward area 16. Water was first diverted toward the smelter, then redirected again by the collapse in area 18.
The surviving passage offers a bypass around the undead in area 12. Nezznar has not discovered this route in the initial state; do not give him that knowledge without a cause.
There is no keyed monster or treasure here. Record the newly known route so it remains available for retreat.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 49; marked map p. 43. Do not add a mandatory crawling damage check.

runbookBeats.title: Area 18 · Collapsed cavern and Vhalak
runbookBeats.tv: Show E18 on entry. Vhalak appears as a male drow until the party discovers otherwise; keep its creature identity private.
read: Water spills down into a broad rift. Ropes hang from stakes along its western edge, while the clack of shifted rubble rises from below. Figures work under the eye of a dark-clad supervisor.

The waterfall fills the rift with a steady roar, broken by the clacking work below. Ropes fastened to stakes on the western side offer a visible means of descent. From the edge, you can examine their condition and the figures beneath before committing to the drop.
ask: Do you observe from cover, talk, descend, or stop the excavation? Who can reach each rope?
run: Three bugbears are here initially: two digging in the rift, one guarding the west side. Vhalak, a doppelganger disguised as a male drow, supervises. If fighting starts, the two below climb up to join.
When two or more bugbears are killed, Vhalak attempts to retreat to area 19 and warn Nezznar. Move the same survivor token and keep its damage; successful escape is not automatic.
The rift is 20 feet deep. Climbing without a rope requires DC 10 Strength (Athletics); failure by 5 or more causes a fall for 1d6 bludgeoning per 10 feet fallen, then prone.
A crushed dwarf beneath heavy rubble wears gauntlets of ogre power. DC 20 Wisdom (Perception) finds the remains; each searching character may make one check per hour. Time spent searching matters.
If these occupants survive and hear fighting in area 19, they arrive after 3 rounds, immediately after the giant spiders’ initiative. Bring only actual available survivors, once.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver pp. 49–50. Vhalak is a different doppelganger from Vyerith at the castle; do not merge their fates.

runbookBeats.title: Area 19 · Temple of Dumathoin
runbookBeats.tv: Stage the temple map privately. E19B reveals Nezznar; show it only on confrontation. Hidden spiders remain off TV.
read: Six cracked pillars frame a hall swept clean of rubble. At the far end, a seated dwarf carved from stone watches over a rough camp. Bedrolls, packs, and a paper-covered table show that this shrine has become someone’s headquarters.

The figures and stonework draw your eye to different parts of the room. You can note where everyone stands and which route remains behind you before answering. The distance between you and anyone present is something to consider while there is still time to speak.
ask: Did the occupants hear you coming? Do you announce yourselves, stay concealed, parley, or enter ready to fight?
run: Initial defenders: Nezznar, two bugbears, and four giant spiders. If warned, spiders hide behind pillars and Nezznar casts invisibility near the table. Roll the spiders’ Stealth. Their first move is to web targets before closing; Nezznar joins on the following round.
If Vhalak actually escaped area 18, it can pose as Nundro for a false-hostage ploy. The real Nundro remains in area 20; never duplicate Vhalak or assume it survived.

Unresolved occupants of area 18 can hear combat and arrive after 3 rounds, immediately after the spiders in initiative. Record the alarm round and relocate survivors rather than creating a new full wave.

Religion proficiency recognizes Dumathoin. DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) reveals the apparent emerald eyes are worthless glass. Detect magic reveals strong abjuration. Removing either eye with DC 10 Strength triggers a room-wide collapse: DC 15 Dexterity, 4d10 bludgeoning and prone on failure, half damage on success.

The table has Nezznar’s exploration notes and maps. His sack holds 190 ep, 130 gp, 15 pp, nine 10-gp gems, and a 100-gp electrum ale mug. Nezznar carries a healing potion, spider staff, and the anvil-headed key to area 20; expended items do not reappear as loot.
Use the following Nezznar card for conversation, tactics, and consequences. Defeating him does not automatically clear the undead or rescue Nundro.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver pp. 49–50; Nezznar appendix B. Trap damage is 4d10, not 4d6. The two temple bugbears are additional to area 18’s initial three.

runbookBeats.title: Nezznar · bargain, battle, escape, or capture
runbookBeats.tv: Keep negotiations on the current map; never show DM tactics or the false hostage’s true identity.
read: The dark elf rests one hand on a spider-carved staff. “You have cost me people, time, and secrecy. Before either of us wastes more, tell me what you believe you came here to claim.”

The words being exchanged do not settle what either side will accept. You can hold your position, ask for a specific answer, or make your own terms clear. The chamber and the route behind you remain part of the conversation, even if nobody chooses to mention them.
ask: What do you demand, what are you prepared to concede, and how will you test any promise?
run: Printed motive: Nezznar wants the Forge and the mine’s secret. He admits being the Black Spider and using both the Cragmaws and Redbrands. In this campaign the Redbrands made Gundren’s capture and castle delivery; do not revert to a goblin-abduction account.

Printed approach: he asks about identities, loyalties, goals, and interests; offers surrender or joint action against the guardians; and intends betrayal once others cease being useful. An offer is not automatically accepted or believed. Let Insight examine a specific claim, and let concrete safeguards matter.

Tactical plan: let webs and actual bodyguards screen him; use cover and the spells on his card. Invisibility, darkness, staff web, and spider climb compete for concentration. Casting an attack or another spell ends ordinary invisibility as its rules specify. Spend slots, staff charges, and the healing potion visibly on the DM record.

Optional DM escape plan: if the fight is lost and a real route is open, attempt withdrawal using remaining resources and normal turns. Announce a visible retreat cue when observable; track destination, pursuit, and stolen items. No automatic teleport, replenished spells, or guaranteed survival.

Capture: decide custody, searches, staff/key removal, bindings, guard shifts, and escort. The printed alive-delivery award is double Nezznar’s XP value total, not his normal XP plus a second double award.

Printed Phandalin consequence: unless the party posts guards, Halia arranges his escape to the Zhentarim before the Lords’ Alliance escort. Stage her actual opportunity; record precautions and let intervention prevent it. If Nezznar dies or escaped earlier, this custody branch does not occur.
choices: Captured: record who holds him and go to the custody/homecoming card.
Killed: preserve the body, clues, and actual loot; other threats remain.
Escaped: record last seen route, HP, resources, followers, and what he knows.
Temporary bargain: write exact terms, collateral, and who observed them; treat future betrayal as an event to play.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver pp. 49–50. Original dialogue and optional escape procedure. Nezznar has no printed connection to Halaster or the custom Echo, and cannot reveal those as established facts.

runbookBeats.title: Area 20 · Rescue Nundro
runbookBeats.tv: Show E20 only after the real cell is opened. A false hostage in area 19 is not this rescue.
read: Beyond the locked door, faded cloth hangs above a simple bed. A dwarf lies bound on the cold floor. His breathing is faint but steady.

You can take stock from the threshold before approaching what lies within. The visible condition of any person here and the space around them matter more than guessing what happened out of sight. You can offer help, ask a question, or check the way out before moving someone.
ask: Who checks him, who watches the doorway, and where can you take him safely?
run: The door is locked: thieves’ tools and DC 15 Dexterity, or Nezznar’s anvil-headed key. Noisy activity here draws area 19’s attention if those enemies still can respond; Nezznar sends spiders to investigate.

The prisoner is Nundro, youngest Rockseeker brother, a dwarf commoner, bound and unconscious after captivity. The book does not assign him Gundren’s stable-at-0-HP state; assess and record his actual condition before resolving healing and care.

Once rescued and able to travel, he is grateful and offers to accompany the party during the remaining exploration. He knows no more about the mine’s layout than they do. Prefer a protected escort over silently treating him as a trained combat ally.
This room becomes a safe, comfortable rest site after Nezznar and his minions are dealt with. It is not automatically safe while enemies remain next door.
If rescued and alive at the adventure’s end, Nundro provides a 200-XP party award divided equally if using XP. Mark the reward pending until survival is known; do not award repeatedly on reload.
choices: Escort Nundro out now, secure a rest, or continue with a stated protection plan.
If Gundren lives, arrange an actual reunion; if he died, let Nundro learn the truth from the party.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver pp. 50–51. Nundro’s rescue, survival, and commoner status are printed; his precise starting HP requires a recorded DM ruling.

runbookBeats.title: Forge use · temporary magic and item custody
runbookBeats.tv: Show only the item and effect the players have identified. Keep hidden chest contents and future hooks private.
ask: Which nonmagical weapon or armor goes into the flame, who carries it, and what will you do before its magic expires?
run: First resolve the spectator’s actual status. Handling or removing its guarded objects can start combat until its obligation ends or it is defeated.

For each eligible item, record its original statistics, bearer, the full minute in the flame, a 1d12-hour duration roll, and campaign-clock expiry. Apply only the temporary +1 attack/damage for a weapon or +1 AC for armor.

Use the Wave Echo journal to record each temporary Forge effect and its expiry. At expiry, remove that temporary bonus and preserve the item; the reminder is not permission to silently change an unrelated item. Do not reset duration on a reload, rest, or scene change.
Lightbringer and Dragonguard are separate permanent named treasures; their properties do not come from the temporary flame process. They remain subject to actual ownership and equipment choices.
Permanent Forge repair, new recipes, and custom Echo reactions are later campaign projects, not free capabilities of this room. Agree and label any house rule before applying it.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 48. The expiry ledger is a table procedure; the printed temporary effect is +1 for 1d12 hours after at least 1 minute in the flame.

runbookBeats.title: Rest or retreat · keep the expedition state
runbookBeats.tv: Keep the party’s current visible scene; do not expose new areas merely by opening this reference card.
ask: Where do you rest, how is the entrance secured, who keeps watch, and are you leaving the mine entirely?
run: Area 7’s northern storeroom is the published secure refuge. Area 20 is safe once Nezznar and his minions are dealt with. Use those facts instead of making every rest a surprise attack.
Before applying a rest, review current HP, hit dice, slots, limited uses, concentration, maximum-HP loss, conditions, food, light, and any recorded class or house-rule exceptions.

If retreating, follow a route actually explored. Ask who assists fallen allies, carries captives or treasure, and secures the area-1 rope. Resolve an existing pursuit rather than creating a new ambush automatically.
Record elapsed time. Check the flameskull’s one-hour return deadline, ten-minute poison durations, and Forge enchantment expiry; recovery does not stop these clocks.

Log the rest or retreat in the Wave Echo journal. If the group returns to Phandalin, preserve the dungeon save. Opening a fresh pack or resetting the session is not the way to continue a partially explored mine.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver pp. 42, 45, and 51; creature/item recovery rules and the selected campaign profile. The rest review is an original table procedure.

runbookBeats.title: Optional · wandering encounters during exposed delays
runbookBeats.tv: Keep the current room and fog. Reveal a wandering creature only when detected.
run: Use sparingly during a long delay in an exposed area. The book allows a d20 check: 17–20 means an encounter. It does not prescribe a compulsory check every turn or every hour.
Then roll d12: 1–3, 2d4 stirges; 4–5, 1d4 ghouls; 6, 1d4 gricks; 7–8, 1d4 bugbears; 9, 1d6 skeletons; 10, 1d6 zombies; 11–12, one ochre jelly.

Roll only the selected count, place the actual encounter, and identify whether it is a mobile existing group or a newly generated wandering group. Never both remove a keyed enemy and add a duplicate of it.
Exclude the explicitly secure area 7 refuge. An encounter is not automatically combat: signs, detection, concealment, parley, or retreat may resolve it.
For the current party, do not pile a random wave onto a major fight just to increase difficulty. Use encounter guidance before committing the result.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 42. Table frequencies and counts are printed; choosing when an exposed delay merits a check remains a DM decision.

runbookBeats.title: Return visit · resume the mine that now exists
runbookBeats.tv: Restore the saved player view. Revealed rooms stay known, but unseen changes stay private until discovered.
ask: How long were you away, what did you bring back, and what route do you plan to use?
run: Open the Wave Echo journal before deploying anything: review room states, surviving enemies and locations, loot taken, opened doors, ropes, barricades, captives, promises, and remaining supplies.
Destroyed creatures stay destroyed except for an actual rule such as an untreated flameskull’s Rejuvenation. A slain Nezznar or departed spectator does not reset when their scene opens.

Possible custom response if warranted: surviving bugbears consolidate around a route they know; a warned Nezznar moves remaining supplies or attempts escape; a discovered entrance gains a watcher. Record who acts, what they know, and when. Do not restore full rosters or invent knowledge of area 17.
Nundro’s condition and location follow recorded events. A delay alone does not silently execute him; if captors make a new threat, establish it in play and provide a chance to respond.
Show observable differences first—fresh tracks, a moved barricade, missing supplies—then let investigation establish their meaning.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver keyed initial state pp. 44–51; survivor response and evidence cues are original DM procedures. They require actual surviving actors and elapsed time.

runbookBeats.title: Before leaving · record the actual ending
runbookBeats.tv: Show a neutral exit view. Publish a recap only after removing private discoveries and unconfirmed conclusions.
ask: Is Nezznar dead, captured, escaped, allied temporarily, or still inside? Is Nundro rescued and alive? What happened to Gundren?
Is the Forge reached, its guardian resolved, and a safe route established? Which rooms or enemies remain?
Who holds each item, map, prisoner, and sensitive discovery? What did the party promise, and what do they want to do next?
run: Record each of the twenty rooms as unvisited, observed, resolved, or unresolved; record actual survivors and hazards separately. Defeating the boss is not evidence every room is safe.

In the Wave Echo journal, record the actual character and mine outcomes, then preview the matching homecoming. Brothers and mine secured, a rescue with the mine unfinished, losses, an escaped Spider, and a continuing bargain are possibilities, not automatic outcomes.
Apply XP or milestones once after reviewing the record. The printed endpoint expects level 5; character sheets change only after the players’ level-up choices and the DM’s award.
Track Nundro’s 200-XP survival award, Nezznar’s alive-delivery award, and monster XP without duplication. If using milestones, note the chosen achievement instead.
Make a restore point and draft the next recap from confirmed facts. Keep Trista’s private token and any unshared clues off the public recap.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver pp. 50–51. Ending branches and room-state review are original campaign procedures; fixed Session 1 facts remain in force.

runbookBeats.title: Phandalin · choose the homecoming that happened
runbookBeats.tv: Stage the neutral town map first. Use the celebratory homecoming art only if the outcome and mood support it.
read: Phandalin’s roofs appear beyond the fields. Someone by the road looks up, recognizes you, and hurries toward town. By the time you reach the first houses, people are waiting to hear what happened.

The places you recognize offer somewhere to begin your account, but the people who hear it will need your words. You can tell them what you witnessed, ask what changed during your absence, or settle a practical need before deciding what comes after the expedition.
ask: Who do you visit first, what do you tell the town, and which news do you deliver privately?
run: If Gundren and Nundro live and the mine is reclaimed: play their reunion and a sober remembrance of Tharden. They can resume stewardship and offer the party a 10 percent share of future mine profits, as printed. This is a share when profits exist, not a chest of immediate gold.
If Nundro is rescued but the mine remains dangerous: let the family thank the party, provide care, and ask what practical support is needed for the return. Do not announce the mine reopened.

If only one brother lives: give that survivor the news and let the party choose memorial, protection, and next steps. Any changed management or profit agreement is a new recorded arrangement, not an automatic duplicate of the printed ending.
If both brothers died or neither returned: focus on telling the truth, returning identified possessions, and settling custody of the mine. No Rockseeker can grant a reward from beyond the grave.
If Nezznar escaped or a bargain continues: Sildar asks for the last verified sighting and terms. Let townsfolk respond to evidence rather than declaring the threat ended.
If Redbrands or Iarno remain active from earlier play, reflect that in town. Barthen, the Lionshield, rescued families, and other NPCs react only to their actual deliveries, rescues, and promises.
choices: Public success: invite the players to describe a small celebration.
Mixed outcome: gratitude, mourning, and practical help can share the same scene.
Unfinished expedition: end on the party’s chosen plan to return.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 51 gives the successful conclusion. The conditional loss, partial success, and escaped-villain scenes are original adaptations to actual play.

runbookBeats.title: Phandalin · a living Black Spider in custody
runbookBeats.tv: Keep a neutral town scene. Private negotiations and planned jailbreaks stay on the DM screen.
read: The cell door closes. For the first time, the Spider’s reach is measured in a few feet of stone. Outside, questions arrive faster than the guards can answer them.

The cell's closed door places a boundary between the prisoner and everyone outside. Questions can wait long enough to decide who stands watch and who speaks. Whatever answer Nezznar offers will still need to be weighed against what you have actually seen.
ask: Who takes custody, who guards him until the escort arrives, and who is allowed to speak with him?
run: Run this branch only if Nezznar was captured alive and delivered. Sildar or the townmaster can hold him for the Lords’ Alliance escort to Neverwinter.
Record seized equipment, any spellcasting precautions actually taken, the key, guard shifts, witnesses, and who is informed. Use the character’s actual remaining abilities if an escape is attempted.

The adventure gives Halia a secret plan to extract an unguarded Nezznar for the Zhentarim. If the party posts guards, their preparation matters; if they do not, establish the opportunity and later evidence rather than narrating an unavoidable cutscene.

Nezznar can answer questions about his operation, but promises and accusations require corroboration. He cannot supply invented authoritative answers about the BELOW token, Halaster, or Aldric’s resurrection.
Count the printed doubled XP value only once for living delivery. An attempted later jailbreak does not duplicate that award.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 50. Guard procedures and investigative clues are original staging of the published custody consequence.

runbookBeats.title: After the mine · level 5 and the next chosen road
runbookBeats.tv: Show only leads the players earned and agree to pursue. Do not display an undiscovered nine-site or Undermountain route.
ask: Do you stay in Phandalin, follow Mormesk’s map, investigate an unresolved enemy, or seek a contact in Waterdeep? What matters personally to each of you?
run: The printed adventure expects the heroes to reach level 5 by its end. Confirm XP or milestone progress and each character’s choices; do not edit all five sheets just because this card opens.

For level 5 and beyond, re-evaluate encounter guidance with the real party levels, numbers, resources, objectives, and terrain. Extra Attack and 3rd-level spells can change a fight sharply; a CR label alone is insufficient.

Use the expanded encounter guidance as advice, with the correct 2014 source profile. Do not increase every old enemy’s HP to erase the party’s progress; add an established objective, environment, or new opposition when the story supports it.

Optional custom continuations: Mormesk’s sewn map can lead to an agreed new dungeon; Dracuseth remains a Waterdeep contact; surviving enemies have unfinished plans. Decide which lead is real before publishing it.

Offer one personal beat each: Trista chooses whether to share the token; Pebble can seek his hammer-makers or a verified mineral lead; Donavan can test a research claim; Ringgo can reconnect with a contact; Aldric can seek evidence about his past. None is a forced secret revelation.
Close with the players’ chosen destination and a short list of unresolved facts. Preserve the finished mine as a place they can revisit.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver pp. 47 and 51: future-map hook and level-5 conclusion. Waterdeep, Dracuseth, character beats, and Echo continuations are original campaign additions. Encounter estimates do not guarantee fairness.

runbookBeats.title: Close this evening · review what actually changed
run: Record the exact stopping room, party positions, HP, resources, concentration, conditions, time and lights. Capture a restore point before closing.
Use Outcome review for rescues, escapes, deaths, discovered routes, promises and item custody. Choose who knows each fact and inspect each proposed quest, journal, NPC or map update before applying.
Record treasure actually taken, not treasure merely listed on a room card. Do not mark a dungeon cleared, reward paid, quest complete or character leveled without its established outcome.
Prepare two or three credible next leads from the reviewed events. Keep unrevealed destination information private. Leave pending phone requests visible or resolve them explicitly.
private: Preparation for several evenings can overlap. Continue the same dungeon save using Preview return; do not generate a fresh floor to resume it.
runbookBeats.tv: Private preparation. Preview the selected player-safe visual, then use Show on TV. Browsing this card reveals nothing.

attacks.name: Fire Bolt
attacks.effect: Ranged spell attack, 120 ft.; ignites unattended flammable objects.

attacks.name: Dagger
attacks.effect: Melee or thrown 20/60 ft.

actions.name: Control Flames
actions.effect: Shape, expand, or extinguish a visible nonmagical flame in a 5-foot cube within 60 ft.; no slot.

actions.name: Mage Hand
actions.effect: Create and control a spectral hand within 30 ft.; no slot.

actions.name: Ice Knife
actions.effect: Ranged spell attack, 60 ft.; piercing on hit, then target and creatures within 5 ft. make a Dexterity save or take 2d6 cold.

actions.name: Ice Knife burst
actions.effect: Cold burst after the knife attack. Target and all creatures within 5 ft. make Dexterity save DC 14; no extra spell slot.

actions.name: Magic Missile
actions.effect: Three darts at creatures within 120 ft.; no attack roll. Each dart deals force damage.

actions.name: Mage Armor
actions.effect: Touch an unarmored willing creature; base AC becomes 13 + Dexterity modifier for 8 hours. Aldric’s AC becomes 15.

actions.name: Shield
actions.effect: +5 AC until the start of Aldric’s next turn; blocks Magic Missile.

actions.name: Silvery Barbs
actions.effect: When a visible creature within 60 ft. succeeds on an attack, check, or save: force a reroll and use the lower d20; grant another visible creature advantage on one roll within 1 minute.

actions.name: Aganazzar’s Scorcher
actions.effect: Fire in a 30-foot line, 5 feet wide; Dexterity save DC 14 for half. Sculpt Spells may protect up to three visible creatures.

actions.name: Web
actions.effect: 20-foot cube within 60 feet; concentration up to 1 hour. Creatures entering or starting there make Dexterity save DC 14 or become restrained; see spell for escape and fire.

actions.name: Knowledge from a Past Life
actions.effect: After seeing a d20 result for an ability check using a skill, add 1d6.

actions.name: Arcane Recovery
actions.effect: Once per day after a short rest, recover spell slots with combined level 2 or less: one 2nd-level slot or two 1st-level slots.

wave-2.terrain: Intersecting six-foot-high mine tunnels and dead ends; jelly can climb walls and ceilings.
wave-2.objective: Navigate the mine while keeping the group together.
wave-2.starting: One ochre jelly lurks in a dead end, then stalks a lone target.

waves.name: Mine tunnels
waves.note: Keep hidden until seen. After a Split reaction, replace the original with two smaller variants at half current HP each.

wave-2.reinforcements: Only Split descendants actually created at the table. No new full-health jellies.
wave-2.nonCombat: Scout together, avoid the ooze, close distance carefully, or withdraw faster than its 10-foot speed.

wave-3.terrain: Thirty-foot ceiling; old skeletons distract attention at floor level.
wave-3.objective: Cross or search the old entrance without losing companions to blood drain.
wave-3.starting: Ten stirges cling to the ceiling.

waves.name: Old entrance
waves.note: Roll one Stealth check for the group; compare to each unaware character’s passive Perception before assigning surprise.

wave-3.nonCombat: Watch the ceiling, retreat, or remove an attached stirge with an action.
wave-3.morale: Each stirge detaches after draining 10 HP or its target dies.
wave-3.retreat: Back through a known tunnel; carrying attached stirges does not end blood loss.

wave-4.terrain: Stone bunks, broken racks, rubble; choose usable cover before placing tokens.
wave-4.objective: Leave, bypass, or defeat the undead guards.
wave-4.starting: Nine heaps of bones; animate in the round after a living creature enters.

waves.name: Old guardroom
waves.note: Describe bones assembling; reveal the nine existing tokens as they rise.

wave-4.nonCombat: Back away before committing, use a different passage, or use undead-specific abilities.
wave-4.retreat: The entry door and adjacent passages.
wave-4.negotiation: None; these are not the Redbrand crypt guardians.

wave-6.terrain: Old stone bunks and a central brazier; partially open door.
wave-6.objective: Cross, evade, or defeat the feeding ghouls.
wave-6.starting: Three ghouls feed on old remains. DC 10 Perception at the door hears cracking and crunching.

waves.name: South barracks
waves.note: Their first visible action is an immediate attack when they see prey; still resolve initiative normally.

wave-6.reinforcements: These three belong to the broader pack but are already separate from the seven in area 9. Do not duplicate them.
wave-6.nonCombat: Listen, close the door, choose another route, or retreat.
wave-6.retreat: Door and known route toward the entrance.

wave-8.terrain: Fungi carpet the cavern; green glow illuminates the room.
wave-8.objective: Cross without succumbing to the gas; this is a hazard rather than a monster fight.
wave-8.starting: Most fungi harmless; crossing the carpet releases a poisonous cloud.
wave-8.reinforcements: Cloud disperses after 1 minute. During that minute, living creatures ending a turn here repeat the save.
wave-8.nonCombat: Avoid disturbing the carpet or devise a crossing method; the DM adjudicates a specific plan without inventing a guaranteed skill bypass.
wave-8.morale: DC 11 Constitution; failure deals 3d6 poison and causes poisoned for 10 minutes. Success avoids both. Review immunity for each target.
wave-8.retreat: Move out of the cavern; leaving avoids later end-of-turn exposures but does not end an existing poisoned condition.

wave-9.terrain: Two 10-foot ledges and central floor with tables; stairs connect levels. Climb DC 12 Athletics; falling 10 feet deals 1d6 bludgeoning and prone.
wave-9.objective: Control approaches, cross safely, or escape the pack.
wave-9.starting: Seven ghouls in the shadows of the western ledge.

waves.name: Great cavern
waves.note: Light or noise alerts the seven; place them on the western ledge and use stairs or actual climbing.

wave-9.reinforcements: Only surviving area-6 ghouls if their actual movement brings them here; there are ten in those two rooms combined initially.
wave-9.nonCombat: Scout in darkness, pick another route, or withdraw using the ledges.
wave-9.retreat: Several exits; show the route the party already knows.

wave-11.terrain: Barracks with stone bunks and brazier. East door barricaded inside; DC 20 Strength to force it.
wave-11.objective: Pass the bugbear checkpoint or learn where their commander is.
wave-11.starting: Five loyal bugbears. DC 10 Perception at a door hears Goblin conversation.

waves.name: North barracks
waves.note: Place all five in the barracks, not as unexplained reinforcement waves.

wave-11.reinforcements: No automatic replacements after defeat. Alert nearby allies only if sounds can reach them.
wave-11.nonCombat: Eavesdrop, deceive with a credible approach, bypass, capture one, or retreat.
wave-11.morale: Published: loyal to Nezznar. DM option: allow surrender if isolated and clearly beaten.
wave-11.retreat: West exit or breached eastern door.
wave-11.negotiation: They guard against undead for Nezznar. Any bribe or surrender is a table choice, not an automatic printed result.

wave-12.terrain: Cold furnace, bellows, ore carts and a 10-foot-wide dry channel, 5 feet below floor. No check to enter or leave channel; it leads north/east under low ceilings.
wave-12.objective: Survive or bypass the guardian to explore farther.
wave-12.starting: Eight dormant dwarf zombies; one visible burning skull overhead.

waves.name: Smelter cavern
waves.note: Stage all eight corpses plus skull. Zombies rise as living creatures enter; reveal before initiative. Review fireball targets and exits.

wave-12.reinforcements: Zombies do not pursue outside for more than one round. Destroyed flameskull returns to full HP in one hour unless remains are treated; track manually from a recorded time.
wave-12.nonCombat: Withdraw, use an alternate route, investigate the channel, or permanently quiet the skull with holy water, dispel magic or remove curse.
wave-12.morale: Ancient orders stop intruders from passing. No forced pursuit across the dungeon.
wave-12.retreat: Channel exits or the entry passage; moving outside does not instantly remove zombies already pursuing.
wave-12.negotiation: The skull follows old orders; any conversation is DM-adjudicated, not a guaranteed release phrase.

wave-14.terrain: Cracked doors (DC 15 Strength), burned furniture, chest, preserved books.
wave-14.objective: Learn, bargain, bypass, or defeat Mormesk without assuming his bargain is trustworthy.
wave-14.starting: Mormesk is unseen until he rises through the floor when a living creature enters.

waves.name: Mormesk
waves.note: Give a chance to answer his demand before combat; use the LMoP-specific CR 3 block.

wave-14.reinforcements: No Create Specter action and no automatic summoned army.
wave-14.nonCombat: Before harming him or taking property, offer something valuable to a wizard and succeed at DC 10 Persuasion. A gift allows books and secret-map study.
wave-14.morale: Protects his treasure. Does not part with the wooden pipe; will trade coins and gems for killing the spectator.
wave-14.retreat: Exit before escalating, but an incorporeal creature is not stopped by a shut door.
wave-14.negotiation: Magic, scrolls, spellbooks and arcane knowledge can interest him. Track the exact promise; the spectator also has a peaceful solution.

wave-15.terrain: Damaged workshop, green-flame brazier, tables and a north room. North door DC 15 Strength; west doors ajar.
wave-15.objective: Gain access to the Forge and decide the guardian’s fate.
wave-15.starting: One spectator guarding the magic items, willing to communicate telepathically.

waves.name: Forge guardian
waves.note: Do not auto-attack; guardian attacks if someone tries to remove items. Resolve two different eye rays if combat begins.

wave-15.nonCombat: DC 15 Deception: claim to be authorized wizards or miners sent to release it. Success sends it home. In this room it also leaves if blinded.
wave-15.morale: Guards its assignment while believing the mine remains in operation.
wave-15.negotiation: Discuss its task and authority. Being polite does not itself end the assignment. Protect the peaceful option from Mormesk’s demand.

wave-18.terrain: Twenty-foot rift; ropes on stakes at west edge. Rope climb DC 10 Athletics; failure by 5 or more falls for 1d6 per 10 feet and prone.
wave-18.objective: Cross, negotiate with, or defeat Nezznar’s excavation crew.
wave-18.starting: Three bugbears: two in the rift clearing rubble and one guarding above. Vhalak supervises disguised as a male drow.

waves.name: Collapsed cavern
waves.note: Start two bugbears at elevation −20 ft. They must climb their existing ropes before joining the upper fight.

wave-18.reinforcements: If two or more bugbears die, Vhalak tries to retreat to area 19. Move the survivor; do not spawn another Vhalak in the temple.
wave-18.nonCombat: Scout the crew, cross via stream/old streambed, parley under a credible disguise, or retreat.
wave-18.morale: Vhalak values warning Nezznar over a losing fight.
wave-18.retreat: Vhalak toward 19 if route open; party through known passages or the stream.
wave-18.negotiation: Vhalak can read thoughts and impersonate; record which identities the party actually verifies.

wave-19.terrain: Six pillars, table, campsite, statue. Removing either fake emerald triggers collapse: everyone in room DC 15 Dexterity, 4d10 bludgeoning and prone on failure, half and no prone on success.
wave-19.objective: Stop the Black Spider, discover Nundro’s prison, and determine the mine’s immediate future.
wave-19.starting: Nezznar, two bugbears and four giant spiders. If alerted, spiders hide behind pillars and Nezznar casts invisibility near the table; spend one 2nd-level slot.

waves.name: Nezznar
waves.note: Spiders try webs before biting. Alerted Nezznar joins the round after they attack; invisibility is concentration and ends when he attacks or casts a spell.

wave-19.reinforcements: Only living area-18 occupants still there and able to hear arrive after 3 rounds, immediately after the spiders in initiative. Move their existing tokens and preserve HP. A Vhalak already here may impersonate Nundro.
wave-19.nonCombat: Nezznar may question them, offer false surrender, or propose a temporary alliance against the undead. The book expects betrayal after they cease being useful; players can secure a real surrender.
wave-19.morale: DM option: seek a bargaining advantage or withdrawal when outmatched; his spiders defend him to the death.
wave-19.retreat: DM option: invisibility or staff spider climb and an actually open route. Neither grants teleportation; concentration and remaining slots/charges still matter. Failed escape leaves capture or combat possible.
wave-19.negotiation: He admits being the Black Spider and using Redbrands/Cragmaws. Keep exact hostage claims separate from proof. Vhalak’s impersonation is not the real Nundro. After capture, specify escort and guards before any Halia complication.

effects.name: Cunning Action: Disengage
effects.note: Movement this turn does not provoke opportunity attacks. Movement, opportunity attacks, Dodge and difficult terrain are checked manually.

partyMeta.notes: Set marching order after Byron and Bowman introduce their characters.

points.title: Neverwinter
points.clue: A great city on the Sword Coast, where Gundren hired the party for the journey south.
points.note: Starting point. This map is an approximate campaign overview, not a measured travel map.

points.title: Thundertree
points.clue: Ruins lie at the edge of Neverwinter Wood.
points.note: Chapter 3 optional branch. Reidoth can help locate Cragmaw Castle. Do not reveal the dragon or cultists on the map.

points.title: Agatha’s lair
points.clue: An old path leaves the ruined village and winds into the woods.
points.note: Sister Garaele’s optional lead. Reveal the exact destination only when the party learns it.

points.title: Conyberry
points.clue: The eastern trail reaches an abandoned village.
points.note: Chapter 3 optional branch; Agatha’s trail begins nearby.

points.title: Cragmaw Castle
points.clue: An old stronghold stands somewhere within the forest.
points.note: DM continuity: Redbrands abducted Gundren and delivered him here. The party has not learned this. Reveal only after a credible lead.

points.title: Old Owl Well
points.clue: Ancient stones rise from the eastern hills.
points.note: Daran Edermath’s optional lead. Hamun Kost and the undead remain secret.

points.title: Wyvern Tor
points.clue: A rocky hill overlooks the southern wilds.
points.note: Optional orc threat from the Townmaster’s Hall notice. Do not reveal occupants until discovered.

points.title: Triboar Trail ambush
points.clue: Here the party found Gundren’s horses and fought goblins on the road.
points.note: Session 1 opening. The party followed the goblin trail to Cragmaw Hideout.

points.title: Cragmaw Hideout
points.clue: The party followed a goblin trail to this cave and rescued Sildar.
points.note: Session 1 complete: Klarg dead, Yeemik left in charge. Gundren’s destination was not learned.

points.title: Phandalin
points.clue: A frontier mining town at the end of the supply road. The party has reached Barthen’s Provisions.
points.note: Current campaign hub. Open the Phandalin town map for shops, NPCs, and local leads.

points.title: Tresendar Manor ruins
points.clue: A ruined manor watches over Phandalin from a low hill.
points.note: The ruins are visible from town. Redbrand hideout entrances and occupants stay private until discovered.

points.title: Wave Echo Cave
points.clue: A hidden cave lies somewhere in the Sword Mountains.
points.note: Do not reveal the point or location until Gundren’s map, testimony, or another credible discovery gives the party its position. Chapter 4.

points.title: Barthen’s Provisions
points.clue: A busy supply shop stands beside the road into town.
points.note: The party begins Session 2 here. Delivery and payment only happen if played.

points.title: Stonehill Inn
points.clue: Warm light and voices come from the largest inn near the green.
points.note: Rumors and Sildar’s lodging; Lost Mine pp. 15–16.

points.title: Townmaster’s Hall
points.clue: A modest public hall sits on the south side of the green.
points.note: Harbin Wester; town notices and orc reward.

points.title: Lionshield Coster
points.clue: A sturdy trading post displays a blue lion shield.
points.note: Linene Graywind; stolen goods from Cragmaw Hideout.

points.title: Miner’s Exchange
points.clue: Prospectors come and go with pouches of ore and dust.
points.note: Halia Thornton; do not announce her private goals.

points.title: Shrine of Luck
points.clue: A small shrine stands near the road and the town green.
points.note: Sister Garaele; Agatha lead if offered.

points.title: Sleeping Giant
points.clue: The tap house has a rougher crowd than the inn.
points.note: Redbrand pressure can arise here; do not place foes until the scene warrants it.

points.title: Alderleaf Farm
points.clue: Fields and a farmhouse lie along the edge of town.
points.note: Qelline and Carp; allow clues to emerge through play.

points.title: Edermath Orchard
points.clue: Rows of fruit trees lead to a cottage on the west side.
points.note: Daran Edermath; Old Owl Well lead.

points.title: Tresendar Manor ruins
points.clue: A ruined manor overlooks the settlement from a low hill.
points.note: The visible ruins are public. The Redbrand entrance and tunnel remain private.

points.title: Hillside tunnel
points.clue: A narrow opening cuts into the slope below the manor.
points.note: Reveal only after the party finds this entrance.

points.title: Ruined village green
points.clue: Grass and saplings have overtaken the old center of Conyberry.
points.note: Custom orientation landmark; the published settlement is abandoned.

points.title: Westward ruins
points.clue: Only foundations remain among the trees.
points.note: Custom orientation landmark. Do not imply a keyed encounter.

points.title: Broken stone building
points.clue: A roofless stone building faces the old road.
points.note: Custom orientation landmark. Let players describe their search.

points.title: Old riverside building
points.clue: A large ruin stands near the watercourse.
points.note: Custom orientation landmark, not a published room key.

points.title: Forest trail
points.clue: A narrow path disappears into the western woods.
points.note: Reveal when the party follows the Agatha lead or discovers the path.

points.title: Western cottages
points.clue: Broken cottages stand among ash-dusted trees.
points.note: Areas 1–2. Keep occupants and hazards private.

points.title: Old inn
points.clue: A weathered sign hangs above the remains of an inn.
points.note: Area 3, Brown Horse. Reveal only what is visible.

points.title: Boarded cottage
points.clue: This cottage is in better repair than the surrounding ruins.
points.note: Area 4, Druid’s Watch. Reidoth is not on the public marker.

points.title: Ruined store
points.clue: Webs and broken beams cover a former shop.
points.note: Area 6. Do not reveal spiders before seen.

points.title: Old tower
points.clue: A round tower rises above the overgrown settlement.
points.note: Area 7. Do not reveal Venomfang before seen.

points.title: Old smithy
points.clue: A ruined forge sits beside the eastern track.
points.note: Area 8.

points.title: Herbalist’s shop
points.clue: A small shop is almost swallowed by vines.
points.note: Area 9.

points.title: Town square
points.clue: A worn statue stands at the meeting of the old paths.
points.note: Area 10.

points.title: Old garrison
points.clue: Heavy stone walls still outline a guard post.
points.note: Area 11.

points.title: Eastern cottage
points.clue: A cottage stands at the far edge of the ruins.
points.note: Area 13. Do not identify the cultists until discovered.

points.title: The Yawning Portal
points.clue: The famous inn is a gathering place for adventurers in Castle Ward.
points.note: Campaign home base. The well descends to Undermountain.

points.title: Castle Waterdeep
points.clue: The city’s fortress dominates the high ground above the harbor.
points.note: Public landmark; city map is a schematic, not a street-accurate plan.

points.title: Deepwater Harbor
points.clue: Ships crowd the quays beside the Dock Ward.
points.note: Public landmark.

points.title: City of the Dead
points.clue: Gardens and memorials fill the walled cemetery.
points.note: Public landmark.

points.title: North Gate
points.clue: The northern road enters the city through its great wall.
points.note: Public landmark.

points.title: Second Margin bookshop
points.clue: A bookshop awaits investigation in Castle Ward.
points.note: Custom Echo Below location. Reveal only after the party learns of it.

points.title: Lantern House
points.clue: A familiar refuge lies among the streets of the Southern Ward.
points.note: Custom hub location. Reveal when introduced.
